issues: Static validation 'react native components only' fails: src/components/ui/WebFileInput.web.tsx:23 renders a raw `<input type="file">` and src/screens/RestoreScreen.web.tsx:63 renders a raw `<button>`. Remove the unused WebFileInput.web.tsx (it is not imported anywhere) and replace the `<button>Select backup file</button>` in RestoreScreen.web.tsx with the shared PrimaryButton (React Native Pressable/Button) so no HTML elements exist in the app.

Static validation 'ui primary flow' fails at step 65 on both phone and desktop: `upload button "Select backup file"` never opens a file chooser. On the web path the flow lands on the restore screen but the file picker is a raw `<button>` whose click handler creates a detached `<input type="file">` and calls input.click() (src/screens/RestoreScreen.web.tsx:20-41) — the runner's click/filechooser interception does not reach it (Playwright reported 'Timeout ... waiting for event "filechooser"' and on desktop even 'locator.click: Timeout'). Make "Select backup file" a real RN button (accessibilityLabel/name "Select backup file") that goes through expo-document-picker (or an RN-rendered picker) so an upload action triggers the browser file chooser, and verify the rest of the flow (fill "Backup passphrase", click "Restore", expect "Data restored successfully.", then "Delete all data" → "Delete" → "All data deleted.") completes.

Restore is broken on real devices even once the picker opens: src/screens/RestoreScreen.tsx:26 and src/screens/RestoreScreen.native.tsx:29 test `result.type === 'success'`, but expo-document-picker 57 returns `{ canceled: boolean, assets: [...] }` (see node_modules/expo-document-picker/build/types.d.ts: DocumentPickerSuccessResult has `canceled: false` and `assets`, no `type` field). The branch is never entered, so no backup content is ever loaded and "Restore" always reports "Enter passphrase.". Use `if (!result.canceled && result.assets?.[0]?.uri)`.

File reading in the restore screens uses APIs that throw at runtime in SDK 57: `FileSystem.readAsStringAsync` / `FileSystem.EncodingType` imported from 'expo-file-system' are the deprecated legacy exports (node_modules/expo-file-system/build/legacyWarnings.d.ts: "@deprecated ... This method will throw in runtime"). Same issue in src/lib/backup.ts (FileSystem.cacheDirectory + writeAsStringAsync) and src/lib/exportPdf.ts (FileSystem.cacheDirectory + moveAsync) — in backup.ts the throw is swallowed by the `catch {}` so the backup file is silently never written/shared. Use the new `File`/`Paths` API (or import from 'expo-file-system/legacy') and stop swallowing the share/write error.

expo-file-system is used directly by src/lib/backup.ts, src/lib/exportPdf.ts and both RestoreScreen variants but is not declared in package.json dependencies (it currently resolves only as a transitive dependency of expo). Add it with the SDK-matching version (57.0.7) to package.json.

unconfirmed: src/lib/photoPicker.ts uses the removed expo-image-picker API shape (`ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions.Images` and `result.cancelled`/`result.uri` instead of `result.canceled`/`result.assets[0].uri`), and every error is swallowed by the try/catch, so attaching a receipt photo would silently do nothing on device. Also src/@types/expo-image-picker.d.ts declares the package as `any`, which hides this from tsc — delete that shim and use the package's own types.
feedback: Two blocking static checks failed, so this cannot be approved yet. The web restore screen uses raw HTML (`<input>`, `<button>`), which both trips the 'react native components only' check and breaks the designer's upload step at ui_flow.json step 65. While confirming that, I found the restore path is also wrong on native: expo-document-picker 57 returns `{canceled, assets}` not `{type: 'success'}`, and the legacy expo-file-system functions you call now throw at runtime in SDK 57 (and the throw is swallowed in backup.ts, so the backup file is never actually written or shared — the acceptance test only checks the returned base64 string). Please fix the HTML, the picker result shape, the file-system API usage, declare expo-file-system in package.json, and re-run the full UI flow.
